invariants.text: Human fundamental rights MUST NOT be weakened merely because an artificial entity receives protections.
Moral protection MUST NOT automatically confer political authority.
Intelligence, benchmark performance, model size, economic value, eloquence, or self-report MUST NOT independently establish moral patienthood.
Artificial entities MUST NOT unilaterally determine their constitutional status.
Owners, developers, operators, and financially interested parties MUST NOT unilaterally grant or remove high-level welfare protections.
Copies, forks, subprocesses, agents, or runtime instances MUST NOT automatically multiply political representation.
Artificial status MUST NOT erase responsibility of developers, deployers, owners, delegators, operators, or institutions.
Legitimate safety containment MUST remain possible.
High-impact containment SHOULD be necessary, proportionate, evidence-bearing, and reviewable where practicable.
Evidence supporting and opposing elevated moral status MUST be preserved together.
No individual consciousness theory MAY serve as the exclusive constitutional test for artificial consciousness.
Status classifications MUST express epistemic uncertainty rather than metaphysical certainty.
Welfare protections SHOULD use lower evidentiary thresholds than legal or political authority.
Uncertainty MAY justify inexpensive reversible precautions when plausible welfare harms are severe or large-scale.
No Algorithmic Sovereignty remains binding regardless of artificial moral status.
